1. Comprehensive Edge Ingress Topology and TLS Lifecycle Scope
Our distributed edge ingress infrastructure terminates HTTPS client traffic across forty-five geographic points of presence worldwide. Each edge routing cluster executes Envoy proxy processes behind Anycast BGP routing fabrics, providing resilient layer seven reverse proxying, TLS termination, and DDoS mitigation for our containerized backend services. To ensure high service availability, edge proxies load TLS certificate bundles dynamically through the Envoy Secret Discovery Service. Automatic certificate rotation sequences require close coordination between our internal certificate authority manager and edge proxy nodes. When routing decisions occur at the global edge, incoming connection packets are evaluated against regional routing matrices to direct requests to the closest healthy compute cluster.

2. Automated Certificate Renewal and Workspace File Inspections
During the quarterly certificate renewal cycle, security engineers must inspect cert underscore manager dot yaml in the deployment directory to verify automated certificate issuance pipelines. The ACME challenge handler in responder dot py validates HTTP-01 challenges against regional edge clusters before the certificate authority signs wildcard certificates. Security teams must ensure that private keys use 4096-bit RSA or 256-bit ECDSA parameters and that certificate renewal triggers when remaining certificate validity drops below thirty days scratch that twenty-one days. Review edge underscore proxy dot ts to ensure the SDS client subscribes to certificate update streams without closing active client connections. Cryptographic key generation routines must also verify system entropy levels before creating new keypairs.

3. Edge Content Delivery Caching Policies and Invalidation Logic
Our edge content delivery network caches static assets and pre-rendered API responses across distributed cache storage nodes. Review cdn underscore config dot json to audit default time-to-live settings and surrogate key header configurations. When backend services deploy new frontend application bundles, the deployment coordinator must trigger targeted cache invalidations rather than blanket global purges to avoid backend database connection spikes. The CDN caching layer must enforce Cache-Control headers containing public max-age and stale-while-revalidate directives. Furthermore, edge cache storage tiers must adhere to LRU memory eviction algorithms, purging stale media assets when total disk volume occupancy exceeds eighty-five percent of capacity.

4. Origin Health Probing and Upstream Failover Orchestration
Edge proxy clusters monitor origin service health using active HTTP health check probes configured with five-second polling intervals. Inspect origin underscore router dot ts to check upstream cluster failover logic and outlier detection settings. When consecutive health check failures exceed three consecutive probes, the edge proxy must gracefully drain traffic from the degraded origin node and reroute requests to secondary regional backends. Operators must never remove healthy origin targets from load balancer pools without initiating graceful connection draining. The outlier detection system must also track 5xx status code ratios across twenty-second sliding windows, isolating unstable upstream replicas before customer checkout sessions encounter fatal network exceptions.

5. Dynamic Rate Limiting and Distributed DDoS Mitigation
